sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·罗森，欢迎收听《重新构想者》，这是一个专注于设计之美及其周围文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 甚至在我还在黑胶唱片时代夜店打碟的时候，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 每天晚上你都要带着 300 件你最珍贵的藏品去上班，你把 DJ 台变成了一个精美绝伦、有 50 年历史的流动快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你喜爱的播客平台上收听来自爱彼的《重新构想者》。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Natalie Kittroweff.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》的我，娜塔莉·基特罗夫。

sentences.en: This is The Daily on Sunday.
sentences.zh: 这是周日版的《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Well, I'm glad I was coaching.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我很高兴我当时在做指导。

sentences.en: I actually just, I had to share this with you guys.
sentences.zh: 其实我刚刚，我必须和你们分享这个。

sentences.en: Last fall, as I was finishing up an interview with my colleague, the politics reporter Robert Draper, he very casually mentioned...
sentences.zh: 去年秋天，当我结束对我的同事、政治记者罗伯特·德雷珀的采访时，他非常随意地提到了……

sentences.en: I spent Thanksgiving in Tijuana, Mexico, undergoing ibogaine psychedelic therapy.
sentences.zh: 我在墨西哥蒂华纳度过了感恩节，在那里接受了伊博格碱迷幻疗法。

sentences.en: ...that he'd just returned from a marathon hallucinogenic drug trip.
sentences.zh: ……他刚刚结束了一场马拉松式的致幻剂之旅。

sentences.en: This was the most radical thing.
sentences.zh: 这是最激进的事情。

sentences.en: Ten hours.
sentences.zh: 十个小时。

sentences.en: I felt nauseous, but they teach you these deep breathing exercises before you go in and you use that to stave off, you know, any kind of nausea.
sentences.zh: 我感到恶心，但他们在你进入之前教你这些深呼吸练习，你用它来抵御，你知道的，任何形式的恶心。

sentences.en: Now, I should just say, Robert isn't exactly the kind of guy I'd have expected to tell me something like this.
sentences.zh: 现在，我应该说，罗伯特并不是那种我会预料到对我说这种话的人。

sentences.en: He's a seemingly staid veteran journalist who covers the American right and the MAGA movement.
sentences.zh: 他是一个看似稳重的资深记者，负责报道美国右翼和“让美国再次伟大”运动。

sentences.en: But he told me this drug was something he felt he had to try.
sentences.zh: 但他告诉我，这种药是他觉得必须要尝试的东西。

sentences.en: Yeah, it was really, really interesting.
sentences.zh: 是的，这真的，真的很 interessant。

sentences.en: I mean, the whole, I have to find a way to write about it at some point.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，整个过程，我必须找个机会在某个时候把它写出来。

sentences.en: The drug in question is called ibogaine, and it's illegal in the United States.
sentences.zh: 所说的这种药物叫做伊博格碱，在美国它是非法的。

sentences.en: But early research suggests it could be a game-changing treatment for a range of conditions.
sentences.zh: 但早期研究表明，它可能是治疗一系列疾病的具有颠覆性的疗法。

sentences.en: Things like PTSD, addiction, even cognitive decline.
sentences.zh: 诸如创伤后应激障碍、成瘾，甚至认知衰退之类的事情。

sentences.en: So today, Robert Draper and I talk at length about his experience on ibogaine.
sentences.zh: 所以今天，罗伯特·德雷珀和我长谈了他的伊博格碱体验。

sentences.en: It's Sunday, April 12th.
sentences.zh: 今天是 4 月 12 日，星期日。

sentences.en: Robert, welcome to the Sunday Daily.
sentences.zh: 罗伯特，欢迎来到周日《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: It's great to have you here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴你能来。

sentences.en: It's great to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能来到这里。

sentences.en: Thanks, Natalie.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，娜塔莉。

sentences.en: So I just want to start by saying that I have so many questions for you about how you wound up having this experience.
sentences.zh: 所以我想先说，对于你是如何最终经历这一切的，我有太多的问题想问你。

sentences.en: I am very excited to talk with you about it.
sentences.zh: 我非常高兴能和你谈论这个。

sentences.en: And I want to recognize that that might not totally be the case for you.
sentences.zh: 我想我得承认，对你来说可能完全不是这样。

sentences.en: This might be something slightly uncomfortable for someone who has made a singular career for himself as a journalist in profiling others.
sentences.zh: 对于一个以通过采访他人来建立自己独特的记者生涯的人来说，这可能会让人感到稍微有些不适。

sentences.en: You are a reporter's reporter, Robert, and I recognize that talking about yourself is not something that you may be used to or find the most fun in the world.
sentences.zh: 罗伯特，你是个记者中的记者，我承认谈论你自己可能不是你习惯的，或者觉得这世上最有趣的事情。

sentences.en: Is that fair to say?
sentences.zh: 这样说公平吗？

sentences.en: That's more than fair to say, yes.
sentences.zh: 这可以说是相当公平了，是的。

sentences.en: I mean, I think that my interest in learning about others is in inverse proportion to the interest I have in disclosing things about myself.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为我对了解他人的兴趣，与我披露自己事情的兴趣成反比。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Well, we're going to proceed with caution in that case.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那我们就在这种情况下谨慎行事。

sentences.en: I want to just start with how you first came to know about Ibogaine.
sentences.zh: 我想从你是如何最初了解到伊博格碱开始。

sentences.en: Just talk about how this got onto your radar screen in the first place.
sentences.zh: 聊聊这最初是如何进入你的视野的。

sentences.en: Yeah, I first heard of Ibogaine from a kind of unlikely source, a former United States Senator Kyrsten Sinema of Arizona,
sentences.zh: 是的，我最初是从一个有点不太可能的渠道听说伊博格碱的，亚利桑那州前美国参议员基尔斯滕·西内马，

sentences.en: who had become aware of its usage in treating military veterans for PTSD and traumatic brain injury.
sentences.zh: 她开始了解到它在治疗退伍军人的创伤后应激障碍和创伤性脑损伤方面的应用。

sentences.en: Sinema decided to try it herself.
sentences.zh: 西内马决定自己尝试一下。

sentences.en: She said, and these are her words, that it was the opposite of a pleasant experience, but it was a really transformative one for her.
sentences.zh: 她说——这是她的原话——这绝对不是一次愉快的体验，但对她来说是一次真正具有变革性的体验。

sentences.en: She'd been working to produce legislation in the state of Arizona to fund clinical research for Ibogaine.
sentences.zh: 她一直在亚利桑那州努力推动立法，为伊博格碱的临床研究提供资金。

sentences.en: And someone who'd done that right before her was, I think, an even more unlikely political advocate, and that's the arch-conservative former Secretary of Energy,
sentences.zh: 而就在她之前做这件事的人，我认为是一个更出人意料的政治倡导者，那就是极保守派前能源部长、

sentences.en: former presidential candidate, and former governor of Texas, Rick Perry.
sentences.zh: 前总统候选人兼德克萨斯州前州长里克·佩里。

sentences.en: He was also into Ibogaine.
sentences.zh: 他也迷上了伊博格碱。

sentences.en: Yes, he was into it.
sentences.zh: 是的，他迷上了。

sentences.en: In fact, he became interested for the same reason Sinema did, that in his capacity as governor,
sentences.zh: 事实上，他产生兴趣的原因和西内马一样，因为在他担任州长期间，

sentences.en: he'd met a lot of combat-afflicted veterans who were sort of at the end of their rope, and he saw what Ibogaine had done for them.
sentences.zh: 他遇到了许多饱受战争创伤、已经山穷水尽的退伍军人，他看到了伊博格碱为他们做的事。

sentences.en: And so he decided to try it himself.
sentences.zh: 所以他决定自己尝试一下。

sentences.en: And, you know, again, Perry, like Sinema, emphasized to me that this was nobody's idea of a party drug.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，佩里和西内马一样，向我强调这绝对不是什么派对毒品。

sentences.en: It was a very, very powerful substance.
sentences.zh: 这是一种非常非常强效的物质。

sentences.en: And I want to get into the power of that substance.
sentences.zh: 我想探讨一下这种物质的威力。

sentences.en: Tell me about Ibogaine.
sentences.zh: 跟我讲讲伊博格碱吧。

sentences.en: What is it, and how does it work?
sentences.zh: 它是什么，它是如何起作用的？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: It's a psychedelic, a drug that is derived from a natural source, actually from the bark of a West African shrub known as Tabernanth iboga,
sentences.zh: 它是一种致幻剂，一种源自天然的药物，实际上来自一种名为西非灌木（Tabernanthe iboga）的树皮，

sentences.en: found principally in the country of Gabon and used in initiation ceremonies in that and other African countries.
sentences.zh: 主要产于加蓬共和国，并在该国及其他非洲国家的成年礼仪式中使用。

sentences.en: But it had been circulating in Europe and the United States, really going back to the 1940s, but particularly so roughly around 1970 when a heroin addict named Howard Lotsoff,
sentences.zh: 但它早在 20 世纪 40 年代就已经在欧洲和美国流传开来，尤其是大约在 1970 年前后，当时一个名叫霍华德·洛索夫的海洛因瘾君子，

sentences.en: kind of chasing the next high, had an opportunity to try Ibogaine and found that it cured him of his addiction to heroin.
sentences.zh: 为了追求下一次的快感，有机会尝试了伊博格碱，并发现它治愈了他的海洛因瘾。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And he began then to advocate for the drug, to help underwrite studies into the drug.
sentences.zh: 然后他开始倡导这种药物，帮助资助关于这种药物的研究。

sentences.en: And so it has continued to exist since then, Natalie, but in the underground because it's a Schedule I drug, meaning that—
sentences.zh: 所以它从那时起一直存在，娜塔莉，但在地下，因为它是一种一级管制药物，这意味着——

sentences.en: It's illegal.
sentences.zh: 它是非法的。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The Controlled Substances Act stipulated that it, like LSD, has no accepted medical usage.
sentences.zh: 《管制物质法》规定，它和 LSD 一样，没有公认的医疗用途。

sentences.en: And so you can't get it legally in the United States.
sentences.zh: 所以你在美国无法合法获得它。

sentences.en: You have to go elsewhere to try it.
sentences.zh: 你必须去别的地方尝试。

sentences.en: And what do we know, Robert, about the way in which it actually functions, in which it has the impacts that Perry and Sinema were telling you about?
sentences.zh: 那么罗伯特，关于它实际运作的方式，即它产生佩里和西内马向你描述的那种影响的方式，我们知道些什么？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I want to emphasize, Natalie, that there have been studies on this, but a lot more studying needs to be done.
sentences.zh: 我想强调的是，娜塔莉，对此已经有过研究，但还需要做更多的研究。

sentences.en: Stanford, in particular, in January of 2024, produced this clinical research of 30 combat veterans.
sentences.zh: 尤其是斯坦福大学，在 2024 年 1 月发布了这项针对 30 名退伍军人的临床研究。

sentences.en: And it seemed to activate in them a type of brainwave known as theta rhythms, which in turn promote neuroplasticity.
sentences.zh: 它似乎在他们体内激活了一种被称为西塔波（theta rhythms）的脑电波，这反过来又促进了神经可塑性。

sentences.en: There's also research indicating that Ibogaine increases the signaling of particular molecules within the brain that have been linked to drug addiction as well as to depression.
sentences.zh: 还有研究表明，伊博格碱会增加大脑内特定分子的信号传递，这些分子与药物成瘾以及抑郁症有关。

sentences.en: So all of these on top of the fact that the study seemed to indicate that Ibogaine treatment can reduce brain aging by 1.3 years per treatment.
sentences.zh: 因此，所有这些再加上研究似乎表明伊博格碱治疗可以将大脑老化减少 1.3 年/每疗程。

sentences.en: So there's a lot of potential for Ibogaine studies indicating that because it enhances neuroplasticity,
sentences.zh: 所以伊博格碱研究有很多潜力，表明因为它增强了神经可塑性，

sentences.en: that it could prove to be a cure for neurodegenerative diseases like dementia, ALS, Parkinson's, and Alzheimer's.
sentences.zh: 它可能会被证明是治疗痴呆症、渐冻症、帕金森氏症和阿尔茨海默氏症等神经退行性疾病的灵丹妙药。

sentences.en: But again, I want to stress that there has been no conclusive reporting on this.
sentences.zh: 但再次强调，我想指出，目前还没有关于此事的决定性报道。

sentences.en: No, totally fair caveats.
sentences.zh: 不，完全合理的警示。

sentences.en: It sounds like a lot of these potential benefits center on the idea of neuroplasticity.
sentences.zh: 听起来许多这些潜在的好处都集中在神经可塑性的概念上。

sentences.en: Can you quickly say what that is and how this drug potentially impacts it?
sentences.zh: 你能简单说说那是什么以及这种药物如何对其产生潜在影响吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 可以。

sentences.en: I mean, neuroplasticity basically means, I mean, to put it in sort of the rawest, crassest way, it's sort of the opening and the flexibility making of the human brain.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，神经可塑性基本上意味着，用最粗糙、最直白的方式来说，它有点像人类大脑的开启和柔韧化。

sentences.en: And where a brain may have shut down owing to a particular trauma, it will, in effect, lubricate or open the molecules of a brain and allow it to become more receptive.
sentences.zh: 当大脑可能因为特定的创伤而关闭时，它实际上会润滑或打开大脑的分子，使其变得更具接受性。

sentences.en: And that has kind of been the elixir enhancing neuroplasticity that scientists have chased for a while in grappling with these neurodegenerative disorders like Parkinson's and Alzheimer's,
sentences.zh: 这有点像科学家在应对帕金森病和阿尔茨海默病等神经退行性疾病时一直追寻的增强神经可塑性的灵丹妙药，

sentences.en: and for that matter, traumatic brain injury.
sentences.zh: 还有创伤性脑损伤。

sentences.en: Fascinating.
sentences.zh: 太迷人了。

sentences.en: It's like the drug, by affecting neuroplasticity, kind of opens parts of your brain that were shut down up, allows you to work inside them.
sentences.zh: 就像这种药物通过影响神经可塑性，打开了你大脑中曾经关闭的部分，让你能够在其中发挥作用。

sentences.en: And, Robert, is the current interest in Ibogaine part of the gradual uptake that we've seen of psychedelics to treat mental illness?
sentences.zh: 而且，罗伯特，当前对伊博格碱的兴趣，是否是我们所看到的将致幻剂用于治疗精神疾病的逐渐普及的一部分？

sentences.en: For example, I know about ketamine being used in therapeutic settings.
sentences.zh: 例如，我知道氯胺酮（K粉）被用于治疗环境中。

sentences.en: I know people turn to ayahuasca, another plant from South America that is used ritualistically for similar reasons to kind of break out of mental health probleMs.
sentences.zh: 我知道人们转向死藤水，另一种来自南美洲的植物，它因类似的原因被仪式化地用于打破心理健康问题。

sentences.en: Yes, and I'd add to that microdosing of psilocybin and MDMA.
sentences.zh: 是的，我还要加上微剂量的赛洛西宾（迷幻蘑菇）和 MDMA（摇头丸）。

sentences.en: And I think that what we're talking about here are not only an exploration of psychedelic for therapeutic purposes, but an implicit skepticism, if not outright rejection,
sentences.zh: 我认为我们在这里讨论的不仅是对致幻剂用于治疗目的的探索，还有一种隐含的怀疑态度，甚至可以说是彻底的拒绝，

sentences.en: of a lot of traditional medications and a viewpoint that had been held for decades that whatever ails you, go to the pharmacist and grab these pills and that's your only hope.
sentences.zh: 对许多传统药物的拒绝，以及几十年来一直持有的一种观点，即无论你有什么毛病，去找药剂师拿这些药丸，那就是你唯一的希望。

sentences.en: There have been intriguing studies done over the last decade indicating real therapeutic usage of these psychedelics, which, of course,
sentences.zh: 过去十年中进行了耐人寻味的연구，表明这些致幻剂具有真正的治疗用途，这当然，

sentences.en: definitionally then flies in the face of the notion that a drug like these should be Schedule 1,
sentences.zh: 从定义上讲，就与像这样的药物应该是一级管制药物的观念背道而驰，

sentences.en: which is kind of the conundrum that the Trump administration is supposedly grappling with.
sentences.zh: 这也是特朗普政府据称正在努力应对的难题。

sentences.en: From what I understand, though, this drug, ibogaine, is much more intense than some of these other ones.
sentences.zh: 据我所了解，这种药物伊博格碱比其他一些药物要剧烈得多。

sentences.en: I want you to just sketch out what's different about this drug from some of the others that we might be hearing of.
sentences.zh: 我希望你简单勾勒一下这种药物与我们可能听说过的其他药物有何不同。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, to put it candidly, I mean, this is it's not a party drug.
sentences.zh: 是的，坦白说，这不是一种派对毒品。

sentences.en: You'd never go to the Burning Man Festival, you know, and do it and dance around a fire.
sentences.zh: 你绝不会去火人节音乐节，你知道的，然后嗑了这个在火堆旁跳舞。

sentences.en: It's, in fact, a drug that is so powerful that you run a real risk of cardiac arrest because it can cause arrhythmia, which is an irregular heartbeat.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这是一种非常强效的药物，你面临着真正的心脏骤停风险，因为它会导致心律失常，也就是心跳不规律。

sentences.en: It can elongate the spacing between heartbeats.
sentences.zh: 它会拉长心跳之间的间距。

sentences.en: And so if you already have a heart condition, you absolutely should not be taking it.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你已经有心脏病，你绝对不应该服用它。

sentences.en: When you do take it, you should have heart monitors hooked up to you.
sentences.zh: 当你服用它时，你应该连上心电监护仪。

sentences.en: You should have professionals nearby.
sentences.zh: 你身边应该有专业人士。

sentences.en: So there is nothing about this that says, you know, woo-woo, we're having fun on psychedelics.
sentences.zh: 所以这里没有任何迹象表明，你知道，狂热地说我们在迷幻药中寻找乐趣。

sentences.en: And in that sense, even before we get to what actually happens to you when you're on ibogaine, it sets itself apart from drugs like LSD or MDMA or psilocybin mushrooMs.
sentences.zh: 从这个意义上说，甚至在我们讨论当你处于伊博格碱状态时究竟会发生什么之前，它就已经把自己和 LSD、MDMA 或赛洛西宾蘑菇这样的药物区别开来了。

sentences.en: Okay, so given that, given the intensity of the experience that we're talking about here, what made you want to try it for yourself?
sentences.zh: 好吧，鉴于此，鉴于我们在这里谈论的体验的强度，是什么让你想亲自尝试一下？

sentences.en: What was it that made you say, like, this could be of use for me?
sentences.zh: 是什么让你说，这可能对我有用？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: I mean, I admit this is not easy, you know, for me to talk about, but I had a very tormented relationship with a very tormented older sibling.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我承认这对我来说不容易谈论，但我和一个饱受折磨的年长兄长有着非常痛苦的关系。

sentences.en: Eli was his name, and when he was 23, he was killed in a vehicular accident.
sentences.zh: 他叫伊利，在他 23 岁的时候，他在一场车祸中丧生。

sentences.en: I was 22.
sentences.zh: 我当时 22 岁。

sentences.en: We were 18 months apart.
sentences.zh: 我们相差 18 个月。

sentences.en: But he was kind of a human wrecking ball.
sentences.zh: 但他有点像一个人类拆迁球。

sentences.en: How so?
sentences.zh: 怎么说？

sentences.en: Well, I mean, my younger brother, who's a psychologist, believed that Eli was a sociopath.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的弟弟是一名心理学家，他认为伊利是一个反社会者。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 哦，哇。

sentences.en: He was brilliant in many ways, but unfocused.
sentences.zh: 他在许多方面都很聪明，但缺乏专注力。

sentences.en: He was this physically immense person, 6'5", and misanthropic, alcoholic, prone to violence, and generally a sullen person.
sentences.zh: 他是一个身材极其高大的人，身高 6 英尺 5 英寸，愤世嫉俗，酗酒，容易暴力，而且通常是一个阴郁的人。

sentences.en: And the household kind of trembled whenever he walked into it.
sentences.zh: 每当他走进家门，家里人都会瑟瑟发抖。

sentences.en: And I was, as the middle child, my parents weren't, you know, they were just doing the best they could to manage, you know, a household.
sentences.zh: 作为中间的孩子，我的父母并不是，你知道的，他们只是尽最大努力去管理一个家庭。

sentences.en: But I was often used as the intermediary, the placater.
sentences.zh: 但我经常被当作中间人、安抚者。

sentences.en: The buffer, it sounds like.
sentences.zh: 听起来像是个缓冲垫。

sentences.en: He and I shared a bedroom so that he would stay away from my younger brother, who he was terribly abusive towards.
sentences.zh: 我和他共用一个卧室，这样他就不会去招惹我的弟弟，他曾对弟弟进行过极其严重的虐待。

sentences.en: And he was abusive towards me, too.
sentences.zh: 他也虐待我。

sentences.en: But, you know, his death and really even his life had left me with not only survivor's guilt, but just a kind of, in many ways, a low self-esteem,
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，他的死，甚至他的人生，不仅给我留下了幸存者的内疚，而且在很多方面带有一种自卑感，

sentences.en: feelings of lingering joylessness.
sentences.zh: 挥之不去的索然无味的感觉。

sentences.en: And I could see tangible ways in which those elements were showing up in my life, you know, that while they weren't, like, causing me to engage in destructive behavior,
sentences.zh: 我能看到这些元素在我的生活中切实存在的表现，你知道的，虽然它们并没有导致我做出破坏性的行为，

sentences.en: I do think that they were, in many ways, holding me back.
sentences.zh: 但我确实认为它们在很多方面阻碍了我的发展。

sentences.en: They were deep thumbprints into my psyche that carried over into my personal relationships.
sentences.zh: 它们是我心灵深处深深的指印，延续到了我的个人关系中。

sentences.en: And so I had not explored this in any really, really fulsome way and saw Ibogaine as an opportunity maybe to do so.
sentences.zh: 所以我还没有以任何真正全面、深入的方式探索过这一点，并将伊博格碱视为也许可以这样做的机会。

sentences.en: Can I ask, what were your hopes?
sentences.zh: 请问，你有什么期望？

sentences.en: Like, as you're going into this process, what are you thinking would be the best-case scenario to come out of this?
sentences.zh: 比如，当你进入这个过程时，你认为从这当中走出来最好的情况是什么？

sentences.en: What are your kind of dreams about this?
sentences.zh: 你对此有什么样的梦想？

sentences.en: What I mainly hoped was that the drug would sort of kind of open emotional apertures in me and connect me more to whatever is pleasant about life,
sentences.zh: 我主要的期望是这种药物能够在我体内打开某种情感孔隙，让我更多地连接到生活中任何美好的事物，

sentences.en: whatever is pleasant about others, would maybe cause me to look at myself in less of a self-lacerating way.
sentences.zh: 连接到他人身上任何美好的事物，也许会让我少一点自我苛责地审视自己。

sentences.en: And to be clear, even though you did end up writing about this for The Times Magazine, it sounds like you weren't originally doing this for journalism.
sentences.zh: 需要说明的是，尽管你最终确实为《时代周刊》杂志撰写了关于这方面的文章，但听起来你最初并不是为了做新闻才这么做的。

sentences.en: Like, that wasn't one of your motivations here.
sentences.zh: 就像，那不是你的动机之一。

sentences.en: To be emphatic, I was not and had no intention of writing about this.
sentences.zh: 我必须强调，我不是，也无意将其写成文章。

sentences.en: So, when a person, you, decides they want to try Ibogaine, what is the process?
sentences.zh: 那么，当一个人——也就是你——决定想尝试伊博格碱时，流程是什么？

sentences.en: Given that it's illegal in the U.S., what are the logistics of making that happen?
sentences.zh: 鉴于它在美国是非法的，实现这一点的后勤工作是怎样的？

sentences.en: Well, I guess to begin with, you better be prepared to buy a ticket because, as you say, you can't get it in the States, so you go elsewhere.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想首先，你最好准备好买张机票，因为正如你所说，你在美国买不到，所以你要去别的地方。

sentences.en: And I think most people go to Mexico, though there are places all over Asia, Europe, and parts of Africa, some of them very kind of boutique-y, very spa-like.
sentences.zh: 我想大多数人会去墨西哥，尽管亚洲、欧洲和非洲部分地区也有地方，其中一些非常像精品店，非常像水疗中心。

sentences.en: But the one that Sinema and Perry had gone to and a number of veterans that I'd interviewed was this place called MBO Life Science, located just south of Tijuana, Mexico.
sentences.zh: 但西内马和佩里以及我采访过的一些老兵去过的那家叫做 MBO 生命科学公司，位于墨西哥蒂华纳的正南方。

sentences.en: And it's not cheap.
sentences.zh: 而且它并不便宜。

sentences.en: It costs $8,350 unless you're a veteran or first responder, in which case they give you $1,000 discount.
sentences.zh: 它花费 8,350 美元，除非你是退伍军人或急救人员，如果是这样，他们会给你 1,000 美元的折扣。

sentences.en: That's significant.
sentences.zh: 这很关键。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: And there are organizations, such as a group called Vets for Veterans, that can offer grants to allow military veterans to go there without having to pay so much money.
sentences.zh: 而且有一些组织，比如一个叫“退伍军人支持退伍军人”的团体，可以提供资助，让退伍军人去那里，不用花那么多钱。

sentences.en: So, once I determined that MBO is where I'd like to go, I reached out to the people there and learned that they have a very long waiting list,
sentences.zh: 所以，当我确定MBO是我想去的地方后，我联系了那里的人，得知他们的候补名单非常长，

sentences.en: but that there are frequently cancellations if you're willing to be flexible.
sentences.zh: 但如果你愿意灵活调整时间，经常会有人取消预约。

sentences.en: And I then said, you know, any chance you've got anything in the month of November?
sentences.zh: 然后我说，你知道的，十一月份有没有哪怕一点可能腾出位置？

sentences.en: This was in, I suppose, August that I reached out to them.
sentences.zh: 我想我是在八月份联系他们的。

sentences.en: And they said, Thanksgiving.
sentences.zh: 他们说，感恩节。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: You know, I didn't have any plans anyway.
sentences.zh: 你知道，反正我也没什么计划。

sentences.en: So, I said, okay, sure, sign me up.
sentences.zh: 所以，我说，好吧，当然，帮我报名。

sentences.en: All right, we're going to take a little break, and then we'll talk about your experience on Ibogaine.
sentences.zh: 好了，我们要休息一会儿，然后再来聊聊你体验依博加因的经历。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson, and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·荣森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周围文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you, and you turned a DJ booth into this, like,
sentences.zh: 甚至早在黑胶唱片时代的夜店打碟时，你每天都要带 300 张你最珍爱的藏品去上班，然后把 DJ 台变成这样一个，类似

sentences.en: living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 充满活力的快闪博物馆，里面摆满了精美的 50 年前老物件。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听由爱彼带来的《重构者》。

sentences.en: Thirty-three presidents.
sentences.zh: 三十三位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning, and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我在凌晨 4 点 30 分给总统打了电话，他接了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 探索太空七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗星星的背后是什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费产品指南。

sentences.en: Today, I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天，我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: Sixty super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 六十款超级圣代。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联盟里最好的球队。

sentences.en: Fifty-three thousand five hundred puzzles.
sentences.zh: 五万三千五百个拼图。

sentences.en: I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都用一个不同的起始词。

sentences.en: Twenty-five thousand recipes.
sentences.zh: 两万五千个食谱。

sentences.en: And I love a one-pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢单锅菜谱，因为我讨厌洗锅。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》庆祝成立 175 周年，帮助您理解世界，充分过好每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 立即访问 nytimes.com/subscribe 订阅并享受特惠。

sentences.en: Okay, Robert, you've made the decision that you're going to go down to Mexico over Thanksgiving to take Ibogaine.
sentences.zh: 好吧，罗伯特，你已经决定在感恩节期间去墨西哥体验依博加因。

sentences.en: Where does the story of this trip begin?
sentences.zh: 这次旅行的故事是从哪里开始的？

sentences.en: What happens first?
sentences.zh: 首先发生了什么？

sentences.en: I took a plane to San Diego Airport and spent the night in an airport hotel, as did the other ten people who would be part of my group.
sentences.zh: 我坐飞机去了圣迭戈机场，并在机场酒店住了一晚，我的十位同伴也是如此。

sentences.en: The next morning, we all gathered in the lobby.
sentences.zh: 第二天早上，我们在大厅集合。

sentences.en: Two SUVs picked us up, and we were ferried across the border, past Tijuana,
sentences.zh: 两辆 SUV 接了我们，我们被送到边境对面，驶过蒂华纳，

sentences.en: and then took a ride down sort of a rubble-strewn alleyway that dead-ended into this compound that was looming over the Pacific Ocean.
sentences.zh: 然后沿着一条布满碎石的小巷驶去，小巷的尽头是俯瞰太平洋的一处大院。

sentences.en: The place looks kind of like a Southwest villa, you know, with a very, very gracious outdoor patio with a swimming pool overlooking the ocean.
sentences.zh: 这个地方看起来有点像美国西南部的别墅，你知道，有一个非常非常优雅的户外露台，还有俯瞰大海的游泳池。

sentences.en: It's like a very, very nice Airbnb, I'm imagining.
sentences.zh: 我想象中这就像一个非常非常高档的爱彼迎。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, I think that's right, with a large kitchen set up to cook dinners for a dozen or so.
sentences.zh: 对，对，我想是的，里面有一个大厨房，可以为十几个人做晚餐。

sentences.en: And you have a sense of professionalism and efficiency from the very beginning that people are friendly,
sentences.zh: 从一开始，你就能感受到一种专业和高效，人们虽然很友好，

sentences.en: but nonetheless, with their own agendas, you know, the first thing they did after showing each of us to our rooms
sentences.zh: 但无论如何都有他们自己的规矩，你知道，带我们看过各自的房间后，他们做的第一件事

sentences.en: was to search all of our belongings to make sure we hadn't brought any drugs or alcohol.
sentences.zh: 就是搜查我们的所有行李，确保我们没有携带任何毒品或酒精。

sentences.en: Our phones were eventually confiscated so that when you're on Ibogaine, there's actually like a danger that you'll drunk dial.
sentences.zh: 我们的手机最终被没收了，这样当你在体验依博加因时，其实就不会有酒后乱打电话的危险。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 哦，哇。

sentences.en: They're protecting you from yourself in this case.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，他们是在保护你免受自身的影响。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Everyone is screened in advance, not only to make sure that they don't have some kind of heart or other condition
sentences.zh: 每个人都要提前接受筛查，不仅是为了确保他们没有心脏或其他方面的疾病

sentences.en: that could endanger their welfare, but also just to make sure that they really kind of emotionally and psychologically know what they're doing.
sentences.zh: 从而危及健康，也是为了确保他们在情感和心理上真正清楚自己在做什么。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: They're ensuring you're committed to it, it sounds like.
sentences.zh: 听起来他们是在确保你对此全心投入。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: And so 36 hours passed before we did the Ibogaine.
sentences.zh: 所以在我们服用依博加因之前，经历了 36 个小时。

sentences.en: And in those 36 hours, there were documentaries we watched, there were Q&As, there were individual sessions,
sentences.zh: 在这 36 个小时里，我们观看了纪录片，进行了问答环节、个别面谈，

sentences.en: and there were group sessions, all of them designed in totality just to make us understand fully, you know, what we're getting ourselves into.
sentences.zh: 还有小组讨论，所有这些的总体目的只是为了让我们完全理解，你知道，我们到底在进行一场什么样的体验。

sentences.en: There was a welcome tutorial documentary that we saw that was hosted by the co-founder of Ambio,
sentences.zh: 我们观看了一部欢迎教程纪录片，由安比奥的联合创始人

sentences.en: Trevor Miller, in which he talked about what was likely to happen, but no guarantees with our Ibogaine journey.
sentences.zh: 特雷弗·米勒主持，他在片中谈到了可能发生的事情，但并没有对我们的依博加因之旅做出任何保证。

sentences.en: And he said that maybe 75% to 80% of you will experience nausea and will end up vomiting.
sentences.zh: 他说，你们当中可能有 75% 到 80% 的人会感到恶心并最终呕吐。

sentences.en: And that's, yeah, yeah, no, I know.
sentences.zh: 而这，对，对，不，我知道。

sentences.en: I mean, vomiting is not my thing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，呕吐可不是我的强项。

sentences.en: I don't enjoy it, but I also had figured, you know, if that's the price that I pay, then okay.
sentences.zh: 我并不喜欢这样，但我也想过，如果这就是我需要付出的代价，那好吧。

sentences.en: And he equated Ibogaine to a roller coaster.
sentences.zh: 他把依博加因比作过山车。

sentences.en: And he said, you know, there will be ups and there will be downs, but the one thing that you don't want to do is try to get off the roller coaster.
sentences.zh: 他说，你知道，会有高潮也会有低谷，但你最不想做的事就是试图从过山车上下来。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So you're there, you're surrounded by these other people who have agreed based on the same premise.
sentences.zh: 所以你到了那里，周围都是基于相同前提而同意来此的其他人。

sentences.en: They are fully in.
sentences.zh: 他们完全投入其中。

sentences.en: Can you just tell me about them, if you're willing to talk about these other folks you were surrounded by?
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意谈论周围的这些其他人，能跟我讲讲他们吗？

sentences.en: Did you learn why they were there?
sentences.zh: 你了解他们为什么来这里吗？

sentences.en: The majority of them were combat veterans, and a number of those suffered from substance abuse and suicidal ideation, in a couple of cases, traumatic brain injury.
sentences.zh: 他们大多数是作战老兵，其中许多人患有药物滥用和自杀倾向，在少数情况下还有创伤性脑损伤。

sentences.en: There was an Army Ranger named Rick who was really, really quiet, and it's said that he had undertaken ayahuasca and tried other things too,
sentences.zh: 有一个名叫里克的陆军游骑兵，非常非常安静，据说他曾尝试过死藤水和其他东西，

sentences.en: but the memories that he had in combat had really been bedeviling him for a long time.
sentences.zh: 但在战斗中的记忆长期以来一直折磨着他。

sentences.en: There was a woman who was from Eritrea.
sentences.zh: 有一位来自厄立特里亚的女士。

sentences.en: She started talking about the war there and couldn't even finish her sentence and broke down in sobs.
sentences.zh: 她开始谈论那里的战争，甚至没能说完一句话就泣不成声了。

sentences.en: And so we were left to imagine whatever she had dealt with before she fled that country.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们只能想象她在逃离那个国家之前经历过什么样的遭遇。

sentences.en: There was a fellow Texan woman named Erin, a corporate consultant, who had experienced trauma that she didn't detail that took place in her childhood.
sentences.zh: 还有一位来自德克萨斯州的女性同伴叫艾琳，是一名企业顾问，她经历过童年时期没有详细说明的创伤。

sentences.en: And so they were, you know, very forthcoming in talking about, in most cases, and I should say that, like you could see, they were wearing it in their physical posture.
sentences.zh: 所以他们，你知道的，在大多数情况下都非常坦诚地倾诉，我应该说，从他们的身体姿态上你就能看出来，

sentences.en: Just this great weight, not only of what had brought them there,
sentences.zh: 他们承受着巨大的重压，不仅是因为把他们带到这里的经历，

sentences.en: but of all of the attempts that they had undertaken before to rid themselves of whatever demons, you know, possessed them.
sentences.zh: 还因为他们以前为了摆脱附身于他们的各种心魔所做过的所有尝试。

sentences.en: I'm imagining people kind of hunched over inward.
sentences.zh: 我可以想象人们那种内敛驼背的样子。

sentences.en: Yeah, it was a really, really somber first meeting.
sentences.zh: 对，第一次见面真的非常非常凝重。

sentences.en: And I think that we were in essence saying to each other, you know, we're all kind of a mess, you know, and we're all here because we're pretty much at the end of our rope.
sentences.zh: 我想我们本质上是在向彼此倾诉，你知道，我们都一团糟，你知道，我们来这里是因为我们基本上已经山穷水尽了。

sentences.en: Okay, so when the process of actually taking the drug begins, what does that look like?
sentences.zh: 好的，那么当真正开始服用药物的过程时，那是怎样的情景？

sentences.en: Take me through that, start to finish.
sentences.zh: 请带我了解一下，从头到尾。

sentences.en: Yeah, the process really begins well before the drug is administered.
sentences.zh: 对，这个过程在给药之前很久就已经开始了。

sentences.en: We had blood tests, heart tests.
sentences.zh: 我们做了血液检查、心脏检查。

sentences.en: We were all fitted with intravenous ports.
sentences.zh: 我们都被安装了静脉输液管。

sentences.en: Each got a couple of IV bags filled with a proprietary blend of vitamins that basically just keeps your body nourished in anticipation of a period when you're going to be fasting
sentences.zh: 每个人都拿到了几个装有专利混合维生素的输液袋，基本上只是为了在接下来你将禁食的一段时间里为身体提供营养，

sentences.en: and your body's going to be undergoing this really, really rigorous experience.
sentences.zh: 因为你的身体将经历非常非常严苛的体验。

sentences.en: It's like you're about to run a marathon.
sentences.zh: 就像你即将跑马拉松一样。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, I will say that MBO does so much of this out of an abundance of caution and as sort of elaborate and even daunting as it is on a certain level,
sentences.zh: 对，我的意思是，我要说的是，MBO 出于高度谨慎做了很多这样的准备，虽然在某种程度上既周密又令人望而生畏，

sentences.en: it's reassuring because they're leaving nothing to chance.
sentences.zh: 但这也让人感到安心，因为他们没有放过任何细节。

sentences.en: So you have this intense 36-hour prep session.
sentences.zh: 所以你完成了这紧张的 36 小时预备期。

sentences.en: Now it's time to take the Ibogaine.
sentences.zh: 现在是时候服用依博加因了。

sentences.en: How do you actually consume it?
sentences.zh: 你到底是怎么服用的？

sentences.en: So we were administered our first of four dosages of Ibogaine.
sentences.zh: 我们服用了四剂依博加因中的第一剂。

sentences.en: It came in the form of a capsule, a big fat capsule.
sentences.zh: 它是一个胶囊的形式，一个又大又饱满的胶囊。

sentences.en: And we were then led down to the treatment room, which is in the basement and is this long rectangular room where there were 11 mats on the floor.
sentences.zh: 然后我们被带到位于地下室的治疗室，这是一个长方形的房间，地板上有 11 张垫子。

sentences.en: How close are you sitting to everybody else?
sentences.zh: 你跟其他人的距离有多近？

sentences.en: About roughly four feet apart.
sentences.zh: 大约四英尺左右。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Something like that.
sentences.zh: 差不多吧。

sentences.en: And so where I was in a corner, the person to my right was the corporate consultant from Texas, Aaron.
sentences.zh: 我在一个角落里，我右边的人是来自德克萨斯州的企业顾问艾琳。

sentences.en: And then directly behind me were two of the combat veterans.
sentences.zh: 紧挨着我身后是两名作战老兵。

sentences.en: And situated in front of each mattress is a mirror and a maraca.
sentences.zh: 每个床垫前面都放置一面镜子和一个沙锤。

sentences.en: A mirror and a maraca.
sentences.zh: 一面镜子和一个沙锤。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: This is so you can like first sit and just kind of look at yourself, have a dialogue with yourself.
sentences.zh: 这是为了让你首先可以坐着审视自己，与自己对话。

sentences.en: The maraca is actually to synchronize yourself with the music that will soon be coming up.
sentences.zh: 而沙锤实际上是为了让你与即将响起的音乐保持同步。

sentences.en: And then to the right of your mattress, in addition to the blanket and the pillow, to the right of it is the bucket for nausea.
sentences.zh: 除了毛毯和枕头外，在床垫的右侧还有一个装呕吐物的桶。

sentences.en: And so we all got on our respective mattresses and then in come the heart monitors and they put the patches on your cheSt.
sentences.zh: 于是我们各自走到自己的床垫上，接着心电监测仪进来了，他们把贴片贴在你的胸口。

sentences.en: And so now you're, you know, you've got a machine that you're hooked up to.
sentences.zh: 所以现在，你知道，你连接上了一台机器。

sentences.en: Does this sound appetizing to you, Natalie?
sentences.zh: 娜塔莉，你觉得听起来有吸引力吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I'm struggling to imagine wanting to be in a scenario where, you know, the first thing that happens is in come the heart monitors.
sentences.zh: 我很难想象自己会想要处于这样一种场景中，你知道，发生的第一件事就是心电监测仪进场。

sentences.en: But I, I mean, I'm impressed.
sentences.zh: 但我，我的意思是，我很佩服。

sentences.en: I'm impressed that you didn't run out of the room, frankly.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我很佩服你没有逃出房间。

sentences.en: Nobody did.
sentences.zh: 没有人逃跑。

sentences.en: Nobody did.
sentences.zh: 没有人。

sentences.en: I mean, again, throughout the evening and early morning, there were people there, about a half a dozen or so medics.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，整个晚上和清晨，都有人在那里，大约有半打左右的医务人员。

sentences.en: And just to keep an eye on, you know, your heart monitor, any other difficulty you may have.
sentences.zh: 只是为了照看，你知道，你的心搏监测器，以及你可能遇到的任何其他困难。

sentences.en: And then at around 11 p.m.
sentences.zh: 然后在晚上 11 点左右，

sentences.en: or so, the lights were dimmed and the music was turned on.
sentences.zh: 灯光变暗，音乐响起了。

sentences.en: What was the music?
sentences.zh: 是什么音乐？

sentences.en: The first couple of songs were music from the indigenous community where Ibogaine is used.
sentences.zh: 头几首歌是使用依博加因的本土社区的音乐。

sentences.en: And the one telltale feature of that music is the Bwiti mouth harp that's played in this very staccato fashion throughout.
sentences.zh: 这种音乐的一个显著特征是布维提口弦，在整个过程中以这种非常断奏的方式演奏。

sentences.en: So I sat there and I started, you know, rattling the maraca along to the music.
sentences.zh: 所以我坐在那里，开始，你知道，随着音乐摇晃沙锤。

sentences.en: And I felt a little bit goofy doing this.
sentences.zh: 我这样做时觉得自己有点滑稽。

sentences.en: And so after maybe 45 seconds or so, I decided that I would stop.
sentences.zh: 所以在大约 45 秒左右后，我决定停下来。

sentences.en: I also noticed I was beginning to get lightheaded.
sentences.zh: 我也注意到自己开始头晕目眩。

sentences.en: We were all equipped with these very heavy-duty eye masks.
sentences.zh: 我们都配备了这种非常厚重的眼罩。

sentences.en: So I lay back and slid on my eye mask.
sentences.zh: 所以我躺下并戴上了眼罩。

sentences.en: And the moment I did so, the hallucinations began in earneSt.
sentences.zh: 我这样做的瞬间，幻觉就开始了。

sentences.en: This is your first inkling, it sounds like, that, okay, this trip is really underway.
sentences.zh: 听起来这是你的第一个预感，噢，这次旅行真的开始了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And as I even mention that, I'm actually getting goosebumps because it remains so present to me,
sentences.zh: 当我甚至提到这一点时，我其实起了一身鸡皮疙瘩，因为这种感觉对我来说依然历历在目，

sentences.en: the sensation of realizing this is not at all what my imagination or what any of the available information had told me it would be.
sentences.zh: 那种意识到这根本不是我的想象或任何现有信息所告诉我那样的情况的感觉。

sentences.en: What was it?
sentences.zh: 那是什么样的？

sentences.en: I'm dying to know.
sentences.zh: 我非常想知道。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, the first were, it was like a film strip, like six images.
sentences.zh: 好吧，最初的画面是，就像一条胶片，大约有六张图像。

sentences.en: And they were all of what appeared to be tribal chiefs.
sentences.zh: 它们全都是看起来像部落酋长的人物。

sentences.en: And then those images dissolved.
sentences.zh: 然后这些图像消散了。

sentences.en: And then they were replaced by new images.
sentences.zh: 接着它们被新的图像所取代。

sentences.en: And I don't remember all of them, but I remember very distinctly that some of them were quite troubling.
sentences.zh: 我不记得全部了，但我清楚地记得其中有一些非常令人不安。

sentences.en: There was a battlefield and there were bodies.
sentences.zh: 那是一个战场，到处都是尸体。

sentences.en: It was drawn across a battlefield.
sentences.zh: 画面横跨过一片战场。

sentences.en: There was another one of what looked to be a lot of starving children.
sentences.zh: 还有另一幅画面，看起来像是一群挨饿的孩子。

sentences.en: And all of these were static images.
sentences.zh: 而且所有这些都是静态图像。

sentences.en: But then the next image that came up was the only one that was not static, which was a pile of rocks and then these long black snakes slithering out of the rocks.
sentences.zh: 但接着出现的下一张图像是唯一一张动态的，那是一堆岩石，然后有长长的黑蛇从岩石中滑出。

sentences.en: Ugh, terrifying.
sentences.zh: 呃，真吓人。

sentences.en: Now, you know, a good therapist will tell you, Natalie, that actually snakes symbolize transformation.
sentences.zh: 现在，你知道，一个好的治疗师会告诉你，娜塔莉，实际上蛇象征着转变。

sentences.en: Terrifying transformation, yes.
sentences.zh: 吓人的转变，是的。

sentences.en: Yeah, right, right.
sentences.zh: 对，没错，没错。

sentences.en: But I did think, yeah, this, you know, this could be unpleasant.
sentences.zh: 但我确实在想，是的，这个，你知道，这可能会很不愉快。

sentences.en: And while I was seeing these things, I was feeling something that, again, no one had quite prepared me for.
sentences.zh: 当看到这些东西时，我感觉到了一种前所未有的体验，没有人真正为此做好过心理准备。

sentences.en: Then my whole body would feel like it was buzzing.
sentences.zh: 然后我感觉整个身体都在嗡嗡作响。

sentences.en: It would feel like that I'd been strapped up to something that gave forth electrical currents and somebody just turned the knob a little bit.
sentences.zh: 感觉就像我被绑在某种能产生电流的设备上，然后有人把旋钮稍微调大了那么一点。

sentences.en: It didn't hurt.
sentences.zh: 这并不痛。

sentences.en: But it's just my whole body was beginning to feel like its neurons were firing.
sentences.zh: 但我的整个身体开始感觉神经元在疯狂放电。

sentences.en: And I noticed my hands began to sweat.
sentences.zh: 我注意到我的手开始出汗。

sentences.en: And so I realized the intensity of this experience is like nothing I could imagine.
sentences.zh: 所以我意识到这次体验的强度是我无法想象的。

sentences.en: And were you anxious at this point?
sentences.zh: 那你当时感到焦虑吗？

sentences.en: I mean, for—
sentences.zh: 我是说，因为——

sentences.en: No, I was not.
sentences.zh: 不，我没有。

sentences.en: Not for a second.
sentences.zh: 一秒都没有。

sentences.en: I actually had this kind of almost clinical fascination as I saw all of this stuff.
sentences.zh: 当我看到所有这些东西时，我实际上产生了一种几乎是临床上的着迷感。

sentences.en: It was more wondrous than it was terrifying.
sentences.zh: 与其说是恐惧，不如说它更让人惊叹。

sentences.en: And I actually welcomed the idea of just completely surrendering to the drug.
sentences.zh: 事实上我很欢迎这种向药物彻底臣服的想法。

sentences.en: When I realized how powerful it was, I thought, actually, this makes the job of surrendering easy because this is not a drug I can defeat.
sentences.zh: 当我意识到它的威力有多大时，我想，这其实让臣服变得很容易，因为这不是我能战胜的药物。

sentences.en: You don't have a choice.
sentences.zh: 你别无选择。

sentences.en: You must surrender.
sentences.zh: 你必须臣服。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And the thing about it is that your mind is very aware of everything.
sentences.zh: 关键在于，你的头脑对一切都非常清醒。

sentences.en: Nothing is muddled.
sentences.zh: 没有任何混乱。

sentences.en: Your mind is quite clear.
sentences.zh: 你的思绪相当清晰。

sentences.en: And so I was having, you know, a dialogue with myself as I was seeing all of this stuff, you know, and asking myself, you know, what does this mean?
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，当我看到所有这些东西时，我其实在进行自我对话，你知道，问自己，你知道，这意味着什么？

sentences.en: I remember one of the first things I saw that had obvious meaning to me was I saw a little piece of what looked like legal paper, and on it was some handwriting.
sentences.zh: 我记得我看到的最初几件对我有明显意义的事情之一，是一张看起来像法律文件的纸片，上面有一些手写字。

sentences.en: And I instantly recognized that handwriting.
sentences.zh: 我一眼就认出了那种笔迹。

sentences.en: It was my handwriting when I was in second grade and when I was just deciding to become a writer.
sentences.zh: 那是我在二年级、刚决定要成为一名作家时的字迹。

sentences.en: And I remember saying to myself, you have to remember this.
sentences.zh: 我记得当时对自己说，你必须记住这一点。

sentences.en: You know, the experience you're describing where you are aware, it has the feeling to me of, like, being awake during your own surgery.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你所描述的这种保持清醒的体验，给我的感觉就像是在自己的手术过程中保持清醒。

sentences.en: You know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 你知道我的意思吗？

sentences.en: Like, you're watching the thing happen.
sentences.zh: 就像，你眼睁睁看着事情发生。

sentences.en: And maybe that also explains why you remember so many of these images so well.
sentences.zh: 也许这也解释了为什么你能把其中这么多的画面记得那么清楚。

sentences.en: Well, I tend to have a pretty good memory as it is.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我本就有着相当不错的记忆力。

sentences.en: But look, this was a 10-hour journey, and I probably remember two hours of it, you know?
sentences.zh: 但你看，这是一次长达十小时的旅程，我大概只记得其中两个小时，你知道吗？

sentences.en: So a lot of it has been lost in the recesses.
sentences.zh: 所以很大一部分已经湮没在记忆深处了。

sentences.en: But there were some things that were just unforgettable, particularly when photographic images came up of members of my family.
sentences.zh: 但有些事情是绝对难忘的，特别是当我家里人的照片出现的时候。

sentences.en: And, you know, I saw my mother, and I saw my father, and I saw my younger brother, and I saw my older brother.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我看到了我母亲，看到了我父亲，看到了我弟弟，还看到了我哥哥。

sentences.en: And there would be images of each of them and of them together, and some of them were of actual photographs in our family photo albums, and some of them were not.
sentences.zh: 会出现他们每个人的影像，也有他们在一起的影像，有些是我们家庭相册里的真实照片，有些则不是。

sentences.en: And then they would kind of crumble, and the faces themselves would crumble.
sentences.zh: 然后他们会开始崩塌，脸部本身也在崩塌。

sentences.en: And then an image of my wife, Kirsten, came up.
sentences.zh: 接着，我妻子克尔斯滕的影像出现了。

sentences.en: And Kirsten's mother died recently, and she's been going through a lot of grief over that.
sentences.zh: 克尔斯滕的母亲最近去世了，她为此一直沉浸在巨大的悲痛之中。

sentences.en: And so I remember actually having a dialogue with the Ibogaine, saying, please don't make her face crumble.
sentences.zh: 所以我记得自己当时实际上在和伊博加因（Ibogaine）对话，说，请不要让她的脸崩塌。

sentences.en: It's just too painful to see that.
sentences.zh: 看到那一幕实在太痛苦了。

sentences.en: And it showed some clemency.
sentences.zh: 它表现出了一点仁慈。

sentences.en: It did not.
sentences.zh: 它没有这样做。

sentences.en: Instead, it just held her image there, a really lovely image of her, and then it was just replaced by another.
sentences.zh: 相反，它只是把她的影像留在那儿，一张她非常可爱的照片，然后它就被另一个影像取代了。

sentences.en: Eventually, I saw images of myself.
sentences.zh: 最终，我看到了我自己的影像。

sentences.en: And those were striking to me because they were definitely not photographs that exiSt.
sentences.zh: 这些对我来说很震撼，因为它们绝对不是现实中存在的照片。

sentences.en: They were instead images of me in a state of almost preposterous self-assurance.
sentences.zh: 相反，它们是我处于一种几乎荒谬的自信状态下的影像。

sentences.en: I seemed so confident, not happy in a giddy way, but just pleased with my place in the world.
sentences.zh: 我看起来那么自信，不是那种头脑发热的快乐，而只是对自己在世界上的位置感到满意。

sentences.en: And it was unquestionably me, but on a certain level, almost unrecognizable.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问那就是我，但在某种程度上，几乎认不出来。

sentences.en: And I realized, you know, in looking at that, the Ibogaine was trying to project for me an image of myself as I should have it.
sentences.zh: 我意识到，你知道，在看着那个影像时，伊博加因是在试图为我投射出一个我本该成为的我的形象。

sentences.en: And to me, that was striking, just as it was striking, that when an image of my brother, Eli, came up, it went quickly away.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说很震撼，正如当我的兄弟埃利的影像出现时，它转瞬即逝一样震撼。

sentences.en: And so...
sentences.zh: 所以……

sentences.en: So did you, you saw Eli?
sentences.zh: 所以你，你看到埃利了？

sentences.en: You saw your brother?
sentences.zh: 你看到你弟弟了？

sentences.en: I did, but he was just one of many.
sentences.zh: 我看到了，但他只是众多人中的一个。

sentences.en: And so, you know, it was as if Ibogaine was saying, that's actually not what we're going to talk about tonight.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这就好像伊博加因在说，这其实不是我们今晚要谈的事情。

sentences.en: We're not going to talk about your brother.
sentences.zh: 我们不打算谈论你的弟弟。

sentences.en: We're going to talk about you.
sentences.zh: 我们要谈谈你。

sentences.en: And what did you, if you remember, what were your feelings when you saw, for example, the images of your family or of you in this kind of confident state?
sentences.zh: 如果你还记得的话，当你看到比如说你的家人的影像，或者处于这种自信状态的自己时，你有什么感受？

sentences.en: I remember I had the capacity to say, that's an unmarred version of me.
sentences.zh: 我记得我有能力说，那是一个未经玷污版本的我。

sentences.en: That's, that's a me I recognize and yet that I haven't seen before.
sentences.zh: 那是一个我认得、却又从未见过的我。

sentences.en: I mean, an image of me that I recognize but haven't seen before is a really powerful idea.
sentences.zh: 我是说，一个我认得却从未见过的自己的影像，这是一个非常强烈的概念。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: It really sort of took my breath away.
sentences.zh: 它真的让我有点喘不过气来。

sentences.en: And now, while all this is going on, I should say that there were these interruptions, you know,
sentences.zh: 现在，当这一切都在发生的时候，我应该说，期间有一些干扰，你知道，

sentences.en: that I'd hear the two veterans behind me were just like this sad Greek chorus of pukers.
sentences.zh: 我听到我身后的两个老兵就像是一群悲伤的希腊悲剧里的呕吐合唱团。

sentences.en: They, it seemed, it seemed like the...
sentences.zh: 他们，似乎，似乎就像……

sentences.en: The worst Greek chorus ever.
sentences.zh: 有史以来最糟糕的希腊合唱团。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But I also, you know, throughout it, like heard things.
sentences.zh: 但我也，你知道，在整个过程中，好像听到了一些声音。

sentences.en: I heard Aaron next to me saying to the medics, this bed is not comfortable at all.
sentences.zh: 我听到我身边的埃伦对医护人员说，这张床一点也不舒服。

sentences.en: I need to move.
sentences.zh: 我得换个地方。

sentences.en: It's not comfortable.
sentences.zh: 这太不舒服了。

sentences.en: I asked her later, you know, I'm so sorry about your discomfort was, you know, did they do anything about that?
sentences.zh: 我后来问她，你知道，对于你的不适我感到很抱歉，你知道，他们为此做过什么吗？

sentences.en: And she said, I don't know what you're talking about.
sentences.zh: 她说，你在说什么呀。

sentences.en: I, I loved my bed.
sentences.zh: 我，我很喜欢我的床。

sentences.en: It was so comfortable.
sentences.zh: 它太舒服了。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 噢，哇。

sentences.en: So I just, I, you know...
sentences.zh: 所以我只是，你知道……

sentences.en: So that was a hallucination.
sentences.zh: 所以那是个幻觉。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: And I was hearing, I heard like another person scream.
sentences.zh: 我还听到，我听到好像另一个人在尖叫。

sentences.en: They did not, in my view, detract from it.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这些并没有减损它的效果。

sentences.en: They weren't so powerful as to make me think, you know, I'm never going to remember this because all I remember is Derek behind me puking.
sentences.zh: 它们没有强大到让我觉得，你知道，我永远记不住这些，因为我只记得身后的德里克在呕吐。

sentences.en: But they were just sort of part of the whole 10-hour psychodrama.
sentences.zh: 但它们只是整个持续十小时的心理剧的一部分。

sentences.en: So when does it end?
sentences.zh: 那这什么时候结束？

sentences.en: It ended at, let's see, I think at 8.30 in the morning when I heard a voice say, it's time for your magnesium.
sentences.zh: 它结束于，让我想想，大约是早上8点30分，当时我听到一个声音说，该吃镁剂了。

sentences.en: And I lifted up my eye mask and saw a shaft of light coming through a window.
sentences.zh: 我掀起眼罩，看到一束光透过窗户射进来。

sentences.en: And I realized then, you know, okay, it's behind us now.
sentences.zh: 然后我意识到，你知道，好吧，这一切都过去了。

sentences.en: And so there was certainly relief for me when it was over.
sentences.zh: 所以当它结束时，我确实松了一口气。

sentences.en: And so they, they hooked us up with a couple of IV bags of magnesium.
sentences.zh: 于是他们给我们挂上了几袋静脉注射镁剂。

sentences.en: And it took about two hours for them to drain.
sentences.zh: 大约花了两个小时才滴完。

sentences.en: And I was hoisted up to my feet.
sentences.zh: 我被扶着站了起来。

sentences.en: And a person allowed me to lean heavily on them until I made my way back to my room.
sentences.zh: 有一个人让我把大半个身体的重量靠在他身上，直到我走回自己的房间。

sentences.en: And that's how I began Thanksgiving.
sentences.zh: 这就是我开始感恩节的方式。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Well, let's take another short break and then we'll hear about what stayed with you after all this.
sentences.zh: 好了，我们再休息一小会儿，接下来我们将听听这一切之后留给你的是什么。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·荣森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重塑者》（The Reframers），这是一个专注于设计之美及其周围文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you.
sentences.zh: 甚至早在黑胶唱片时代的夜总会当DJ时，你每晚都要带着300件你最珍视的宝贝去上班。

sentences.en: And you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你把一个DJ台变成了一个充满50年历史精美文物的流动快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你喜爱的播客平台上收听来自爱彼（Audemars Piguet）的《重塑者》。

sentences.en: I'm Wynna Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是刘芸娜（Wynna Liu）。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我编写了“连线”（Connections）游戏，这是《纽约时报》游戏板块的谜题之一。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢试图捉弄你。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖斯基（Sam Mazursky）。

sentences.en: And I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我每天都创作“拼字蜜蜂”（Spelling Bee）和“字母箱”（Letterboxd）游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做联觉（promesthesia）的特质。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 当我听音乐时我能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像你刚刚听到的这些人一样的人制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com/games 从今天开始游玩。

sentences.en: Okay, Robert, you had just gone on this trip for an entire night.
sentences.zh: 好了，罗伯特，你刚刚经历了一整晚的这种旅程。

sentences.en: How did you feel?
sentences.zh: 你感觉怎么样？

sentences.en: Like crap.
sentences.zh: 糟透了。

sentences.en: I really felt terrible.
sentences.zh: 我真的感觉糟糕极了。

sentences.en: I mean, in fact, I struggled to think of a day when I felt physically worse than the one I did on what they call, with lovely understatement, gray day, a day of introspection.
sentences.zh: 我是说，事实上，我很难想出一个日子的身体感觉能比他们用委婉优美的说法称之为“灰色日子”——一个内省的日子——那天更糟糕了。

sentences.en: Gray day.
sentences.zh: 灰色日子。

sentences.en: Yeah, it was actually the only introspection I was undergoing was, why the hell did I do this to myself?
sentences.zh: 对，实际上我当时唯一的内省是，我他妈为什么要对自己做这种事？

sentences.en: Because, I mean, you're, it felt as if, you know, I'd been kind of run through a shredder or something.
sentences.zh: 因为，我是说，你，感觉就像是，你知道，我被放进碎纸机里搅了一遭或者别的什么。

sentences.en: When I closed my eyes, I was still seeing hallucinations.
sentences.zh: 当我闭上眼睛时，我仍然能看到幻觉。

sentences.en: I was still seeing the film strips of images.
sentences.zh: 我仍然看到一幅幅影像的胶片条。

sentences.en: Yikes.
sentences.zh: 哎呀。

sentences.en: And I could barely stand on my own power.
sentences.zh: 我几乎无法靠自己的力量站立。

sentences.en: I could barely walk.
sentences.zh: 我几乎走不动路。

sentences.en: And I thought, you know, tomorrow evening, you know, it's going to be my last evening here.
sentences.zh: 我想，你知道，明天晚上，你知道，这将是我在这里的最后一个晚上。

sentences.en: And then the morning after that, I head back.
sentences.zh: 然后接下来的那个早晨，我就要回去了。

sentences.en: And I, if I'm like this, I can't function.
sentences.zh: 如果我一直是这个状态，我就无法正常生活。

sentences.en: The New York Times is going to fire me.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》要解雇我了。

sentences.en: My wife is going to divorce me.
sentences.zh: 我妻子要和我离婚了。

sentences.en: I mean, I'm just going to be like this worthless pineapple of a human being.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我简直要变成一个毫无价值的废人。

sentences.en: And, and, uh...
sentences.zh: 而且，呃……

sentences.en: You're basically in the midst of what sounds like the worst hangover ever.
sentences.zh: 你基本上正处于听起来是有史以来最糟糕的宿醉之中。

sentences.en: You're struggling.
sentences.zh: 你在苦苦挣扎。

sentences.en: You're struggling.
sentences.zh: 你在苦苦挣扎。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I struggled.
sentences.zh: 我苦苦挣扎。

sentences.en: And I, ultimately, after being unable to have dinner, went to sleep Thanksgiving evening and woke up the next morning at 6.30 just feeling like a million dollars.
sentences.zh: 最终，在无法吃晚饭后，我在感恩节的晚上入睡了，并在第二天早上6点30分醒来，感觉好极了。

sentences.en: I mean, I was, I was stunned by how good I was.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我，我被我自己的状态惊艳到了。

sentences.en: And my body no longer ate.
sentences.zh: 而且我的身体不再难受了。

sentences.en: There were no longer any hallucinations.
sentences.zh: 幻觉也完全消失了。

sentences.en: The drug had moved its way out of the system and really felt terrific.
sentences.zh: 药物已经排出了体外，感觉真的棒极了。

sentences.en: And as did all of the others.
sentences.zh: 其他人也是如此。

sentences.en: And so, that afternoon, we were given an opportunity on what would be our final day there to try yet another psychedelic.
sentences.zh: 因此，那天下午，在我们在那里的最后一天，我们得到了一个尝试另一种迷幻药的机会。

sentences.en: It is called 5-M-E-O-D-M-T, which is a drug that is derived from the toxic secretions of the Sonoran Desert Toad.
sentences.zh: 它被称为5-MeO-DMT，这种药物提取自索诺拉沙漠蟾蜍的有毒分泌物。

sentences.en: And it's a very, very intense, but also short-lived drug.
sentences.zh: 这是一种非常、非常强烈，但也很短暂的药物。

sentences.en: It only lasts about 10 minutes or so.
sentences.zh: 它只持续大约10分钟左右。

sentences.en: Still, right when you're feeling better, they're offering you another opportunity.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，就在你感觉好一点的时候，他们又给了你一次机会。

sentences.en: Well, the truth is, you know, that, I mean, everyone felt better that day than they did on their gray day.
sentences.zh: 嗯，事实是，你知道，我的意思是，那天每个人都比他们阴郁的那天感觉更好。

sentences.en: But a number of the people didn't feel so well.
sentences.zh: 但也有一些人感觉没那么好。

sentences.en: They had a very, very rickety, to say the least, ibogaine experience.
sentences.zh: 温和地说，他们的伊博加因体验非常、非常不稳定。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 哈。

sentences.en: And what 5-M-E-O-D-M-T has been described as is it's almost a euphoria-inducing drug that has the effect of sanding off the very rough edges of your ibogaine experience.
sentences.zh: 而据描述，5-MeO-DMT几乎是一种能诱发欣快感的药物，它的作用是抹平你伊博加因体验中非常尖锐的棱角。

sentences.en: And so.
sentences.zh: 所以。

sentences.en: And is that what it was?
sentences.zh: 情况真的是这样吗？

sentences.en: What was it like?
sentences.zh: 那是一种什么样的感觉？

sentences.en: Well, it comes, the drug does, in the form of something you smoke.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这种药是以抽吸的形式使用的。

sentences.en: Someone gives you this long-stemmed pipe, and you breathe in deeply, and then you fall back with an eye mask on.
sentences.zh: 有人递给你一个长柄烟斗，你深吸一口气，然后戴着眼罩向后倒下。

sentences.en: And at first, I didn't know what to make of the drug.
sentences.zh: 起初，我不知道该怎么看待这种药。

sentences.en: I was still hyper-conscious of the fact that I hadn't eaten much in the last day and a half.
sentences.zh: 我仍然过分地意识到这样一个事实：在过去的一天半里我没有吃多少东西。

sentences.en: My mind was just, you know, racing about.
sentences.zh: 我的脑子里只是，你知道，思绪万千。

sentences.en: And at a certain point, I started rubbing my cheSt.
sentences.zh: 在某个时刻，我开始揉搓我的胸口。

sentences.en: And it's something that I do right around my solar plexus, almost as if I'm trying to kind of push away something or protect myself from something.
sentences.zh: 这是我在太阳神经丛附近常做的一个动作，几乎就像我在试图推开什么东西，或者保护自己免受什么东西的伤害。

sentences.en: You do that generally, you're saying?
sentences.zh: 你是说你平时也会这样做？

sentences.en: Yeah, I do that generally.
sentences.zh: 是的，我平时会这样做。

sentences.en: But then I just then, while lying there, had this memory of a photograph that my younger brother had unearthed recently,
sentences.zh: 但随后就在那时，当我躺在那里时，我突然记起了一张我弟弟最近翻出来照片，

sentences.en: which was a photo of me probably at the age of like four or three.
sentences.zh: 那是一张我大概三四岁时的照片。

sentences.en: And it was me and my brother Eli on the lawn of our house in Houston, and he was lying on top of me.
sentences.zh: 照片上是我和弟弟伊利在我家位于休斯顿的草坪上，他趴在我身上。

sentences.en: Whoa.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: My mother had taken the photograph, and it was clear that she wouldn't be taking a photograph of me if he was, like, beating the crap out of me.
sentences.zh: 这张照片是我妈妈拍的，很显然，如果他像是在把我往死里打的话，她就不会给我拍照了。

sentences.en: But you can also see that my face looks alarmed, and I look like I'm being suffocated.
sentences.zh: 但你也能看到我的脸看起来很惊恐，我看起来快要窒息了。

sentences.en: Whoa, Robert.
sentences.zh: 哇，罗伯特。

sentences.en: But from there, my mind suddenly jumped forward in time to my years as a, say, 12 or 13-year-old, when my older brother would have me on the ground, his knees on my upper arms,
sentences.zh: 但从那里开始，我的思绪突然向前跃进到我大概12、13岁的岁月，那时我哥哥会把我按在地上，他的膝盖压在我的大臂上，

sentences.en: pinned to the ground, and hitting me in the solar plexus with his fingers.
sentences.zh: 把我按倒在地上，用手指击打我的太阳神经丛。

sentences.en: He was doing that repeatedly to me, as he had done.
sentences.zh: 他像以前一样，一遍又一遍地对我这样做。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I began to make this connection then, this very physical connection, to this thing that I often do.
sentences.zh: 然后我开始把这种联系建立起来，这种非常身体上的联系，和我经常做的这个动作联系起来。

sentences.en: And it was really a startling reminder of how present he was as a kind of physical and violent force in my life when I had spent so much time more thinking about the tragedy of him dying so young.
sentences.zh: 这真是一个令人震惊的提醒，提醒我当我在他英年早逝的悲剧上花了那么多时间去思考时，他在我的生活中作为一个实体和暴力力量是多么真实的存在。

sentences.en: Rather than what he had inflicted on me and on my younger brother.
sentences.zh: 而不是去想他对我和我弟弟施加了什么。

sentences.en: And suddenly you're on this trip, and you're having this vision that leads you to another vision, and you're realizing all of this.
sentences.zh: 突然之间你处于这场迷幻之旅中，你有了这个幻象，它引导你走向另一个幻象，你意识到了所有这些。

sentences.en: Like, that motion that I do to myself is connected to this experience of what, I mean, you called it torture, what sounds like trauma.
sentences.zh: 比如，我对自己做的那个动作，与这种经历有关——我的意思是，你称之为折磨，听起来像是创伤。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I can think about moments in the present day where I've rubbed my solar plexus, and it's usually in moments of stress or a moment where I'm feeling some discomfort.
sentences.zh: 我能想起现在生活中我揉搓太阳神经丛的时刻，那通常是在压力时刻，或者是我感到有些不适的时刻。

sentences.en: I'm feeling him on me, I'm now realizing.
sentences.zh: 我意识到，我现在能感觉到他在我身上。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And so that was a pretty sort of startling thing.
sentences.zh: 所以这真是一件相当令人震惊的事情。

sentences.en: It felt very much like a kind of psychic bookend had been presented before me.
sentences.zh: 感觉非常像是一种心理上的句号摆在了我的面前。

sentences.en: So, I have to ask, what was it like returning home after all this?
sentences.zh: 所以，我不得不问，经历这一切后回到家是什么感觉？

sentences.en: I did feel, in the first few days in particular, almost like walking around in a spacesuit, you know, on the moon or something.
sentences.zh: 特别是最初的几天，我确实感觉像是在月球或什么地方穿着宇航服走来走去。

sentences.en: You know, just still not quite sure how to relate the experience that I'd had to all the phenomena around me.
sentences.zh: 你知道，还是不太确定该如何将我的这段经历与我周围的所有现象联系起来。

sentences.en: Did you feel heavy?
sentences.zh: 你觉得身体沉重吗？

sentences.en: No, no, I did not.
sentences.zh: 不，不，我没有。

sentences.en: No, I felt sort of more gravity-defying, but recognizing that gravity is there, and at some point I will have to succumb to it.
sentences.zh: 不，我感觉更像是无视重力，但也意识到重力就在那里，在某个时刻我将不得不向它屈服。

sentences.en: The drug stays in your system in terms of what it does to your neural pathways for a period, you know, for over a month.
sentences.zh: 就它对你的神经通路的作用而言，这种药物会在你的体内停留一段时间，你知道，超过一个月。

sentences.en: And you're returning to, invariably, you know, to real life with all that that means.
sentences.zh: 而你不可避免地要带着这一切回归现实生活。

sentences.en: And so I've just had to kind of let this integrate itself into the demands of my everyday existence.
sentences.zh: 所以我不得不让这种体验融入我日常生活的种种需求中。

sentences.en: What about that neuroplasticity piece that we talked about?
sentences.zh: 我们讨论过的那部分神经可塑性呢？

sentences.en: Like, do you feel that in yourself, that you had parts of your own mind opened in some way, that you were able to see yourself differently?
sentences.zh: 比如，你在自己身上感受到了吗，你心灵的某些部分在某种程度上被打开了，你能够以不同的方式看待自己？

sentences.en: I'm thinking of, obviously, the image of you at your most confident.
sentences.zh: 我显然想到了你最自信时的那个形象。

sentences.en: Like, did that remain?
sentences.zh: 比如，那种状态保留下来了吗？

sentences.en: Did that unlock something?
sentences.zh: 这是否解开了什么心结？

sentences.en: Yes, but, is what I would say.
sentences.zh: 我想说的是，是的。

sentences.en: I mean, like so many therapeutic treatments, I think there's always the prospect of backsliding.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，就像许多治疗方法一样，我认为总是存在着退步的前景。

sentences.en: A moment where, you know, you run into conflict and feel the worst of yourself rising up in you.
sentences.zh: 一个你知道你会遇到冲突并感到自己最糟糕的一面在体内滋生的时刻。

sentences.en: What has happened with me is that it has spurred a different kind of internal dialogue in me that I'm still at pains to describe how it differentiates itself from whatever the usual blah,
sentences.zh: 发生在我身上的改变是，它激发了我体内一种不同类型的内心对话，我仍然很难描述它与我内心通常那些废话、

sentences.en: blah, blah inside me is taking place.
sentences.zh: 废话、废话有什么不同。

sentences.en: But I do have, like, you know, more searching questions of why did I do that or how am I letting this affect my own self-regard?
sentences.zh: 但我确实会提出更多探究性的问题，比如我为什么那样做，或者我是如何让这件事影响我对自己的看法的？

sentences.en: And it has definitely added a kind of depth to how I regard the outside world and my place in it.
sentences.zh: 它绝对为我如何看待外部世界以及我在其中的位置增加了一种深度。

sentences.en: There is, you know, a space, a journey that connects, you know,
sentences.zh: 你知道，有一个空间，一段旅程，它将，你知道，

sentences.en: the kid on the grass with a brother on top of him to this sort of transfigured image of this other version of me that is out from under that earlier predicament.
sentences.zh: 草地上那个被哥哥压在身上的小孩，连接到了另一个版本的我的那种超脱的形象，那个摆脱了早期困境的我。

sentences.en: That's free.
sentences.zh: 那个自由的我。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so that's, I suppose, you know, the journey that I've been on.
sentences.zh: 所以我想，这就是我一直在经历的旅程。

sentences.en: But understanding both points, the beginning point and the end point, is a clarifying and useful experience for me.
sentences.zh: 但理解这两个节点——起点和终点，对我来说是一次清晰且有益的体验。

sentences.en: Well, Robert, thank you for letting us into your journey and for sharing everything you did.
sentences.zh: 好的，罗伯特，谢谢你让我们走进你的旅程，并分享了你所经历的一切。

sentences.en: We really appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们真的很感激。

sentences.en: Sure thing, Natalie.
sentences.zh: 不客气，娜塔莉。

sentences.zh: 今天的节目由蒂娜·安托利尼制作，亚历克斯·巴伦提供了帮助。

sentences.en: It was edited by Wendy Doerr and engineered by Rowan Nemistow.
sentences.zh: 由温迪·多尔剪辑，罗温·内米斯托担任音频工程。

sentences.en: It contains music by Marion Lozano, Rowan Nemistow, Dan Powell, and Diane Wong.
sentences.zh: 其中包含马里昂·洛萨诺、罗温·内米斯托、丹·鲍威尔和黛安·王创作的音乐。

sentences.zh: 我们的制作经理是弗兰尼·卡托斯。

sentences.zh: 这就是《今日早报》的全部内容。

sentences.zh: 我是娜塔莉·基特罗维斯。

sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·荣森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一个专注于设计之爱及其周围文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you.
sentences.zh: 早在黑胶唱片时代我在夜总会打碟的时候，你每晚都要带着300件你最珍贵的传家宝去上班。

sentences.en: And you turned a DJ booth into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你把一个打碟台变成了一个充满活力的、由美丽50年历史藏品组成的快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听来自爱彼的《重构者》。
